source.title: Romance of the Three Kingdoms (San kuo yan yi)
source.author: Attributed to Luo Guanzhong (14th century); English translation by C. H. Brewitt-Taylor
source.first_published: Chinese original 14th century (1522 edition); Brewitt-Taylor translation Kelly & Walsh, Shanghai, 1925
source.edition_used: Project Gutenberg eBook #77416, 'San kuo; or, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, volume 1 of 2' (chapters 1–60), released 7 Dec 2025. Player-facing text paraphrases the translation; names are given in pinyin instead of the translation's Wade-Giles. All Project Gutenberg references must be removed before release.
source.rights_note: Chinese original: public domain everywhere. Translation published 1925: public domain in the US (Gutenberg marks it so); the translator died in 1938, so it is also out of copyright in life+70 countries. The product lead chose this book for an internal prototype on 2026-10-16; formal sign-off still goes through the review checklist before any public release. Only volume 1 (ch1–60) was located; volume 2 must be checked separately before using later chapters. Avoid the look of any TV series, film, comic or video game adaptation (e.g. the 1994 CCTV series, Red Cliff (2008), Koei's Dynasty Warriors / Romance of the Three Kingdoms games). Pack text has not yet been checked line by line against the Brewitt-Taylor chapters (the full text could not be loaded in this environment).

book_bible.setting: China at the end of the Han dynasty, about 184–220 AD: a puppet emperor, warlords carving up the empire, and three states (Wei, Shu, Wu) rising out of the wars. Palaces in the capital Xuchang, river camps on the Yangtze, mountain roads in winter.
book_bible.tone: Epic, political and personal at once: oaths, debts of honour, stratagems and bluffs. Battles are told briskly and without gore; the drama is in who outwits, persuades or spares whom.

main_characters.name: Liu Bei (Xuande)
main_characters.role: Distant kinsman of the Han emperor; founder of Shu
main_characters.age_note: Adult; historical birth year 161 (not stated in the novel)

main_characters.name: Guan Yu (Yunchang)
main_characters.role: Liu Bei's sworn brother; a general famous for loyalty
main_characters.age_note: Adult (novel: sworn brother at the Peach Garden oath)

main_characters.name: Zhang Fei (Yide)
main_characters.role: Liu Bei's sworn brother; fierce and impulsive

main_characters.name: Cao Cao (Mengde)
main_characters.role: Prime Minister who controls the emperor; founder of Wei

main_characters.name: Zhuge Liang (Kongming)
main_characters.age_note: Adult, 27 in 208 AD (historical; the novel calls him young but grown)

main_characters.name: Zhou Yu (Gongjin)
main_characters.role: Commander-in-chief of Wu at Red Cliffs

main_characters.name: Lu Su (Zijing)
main_characters.role: Wu adviser; honest go-between for Wu and Liu Bei

main_characters.name: Zhang Liao (Wenyuan)
main_characters.role: Cao Cao's general; old friend of Guan Yu

main_characters.name: Liu Shan (A Dou)
main_characters.role: Liu Bei's infant son, rescued at Changban

segments.title: Oath in the Peach Garden
segments.summary: Liu Bei meets Zhang Fei and Guan Yu at a recruiting notice and the three swear brotherhood in a peach garden.
segments.core_question: Will these two strangers trust you enough to swear brotherhood?
segments.why_this_template: A short conversation: the player learns who the two men are and what they want before proposing the oath.
segments.interactive_hook: Choosing what to say about yourself to two hot-tempered strangers.
key_choices: Admit your poverty or boast of your royal blood
segments.canon_anchor: The oath always happens; only the tone of the first meeting differs.

segments.title: The Seven-Jewelled Sword
segments.summary: Cao Cao takes a jewelled dagger into Dong Zhuo's chamber to kill the tyrant, is nearly caught, and turns it into a gift.
segments.core_question: Can you get out of Dong Zhuo's chamber alive with the dagger in your hand?
segments.why_this_template: Timing and bluffing with objects: the mirror, the dagger, the horse.
segments.interactive_hook: The player discovers the famous bluff ('a gift for you') themselves.
segments.canon_anchor: Any ending leads to Cao Cao fleeing the capital, as in the novel.

segments.title: Heroes Over Green Plums
segments.summary: Cao Cao invites Liu Bei, who has secretly joined a plot against him, to drink warm wine over green plums and asks who the true heroes of the age are.
segments.core_question: Can you hide your ambition from the most suspicious man in the empire, and get out of his capital?
segments.why_this_template: This is a social survival scene: the player manages one powerful man's suspicion through what they say and how they react, and the 'relationship' is measured as suspicion rather than warmth.
segments.interactive_hook: Every answer is a bluff. The famous moment, dropped chopsticks covered by a crack of thunder, becomes the player's own split-second save.
key_choices: Cover for your sworn brothers' drawn swords
Ask for an army to leave the capital
segments.canon_anchor: If Cao Cao keeps Liu Bei close, the next segment still opens with Liu Bei leaving the capital on campaign; the 'if' ending only colours how he left.

segments.title: Three Conditions
segments.summary: Cut off from Liu Bei, Guan Yu agrees to stay with Cao Cao on three conditions, refuses every gift, and finally rides away to find his brother.
segments.core_question: How do you accept Cao Cao's hospitality without being bought?
segments.why_this_template: Repeated offers from Cao Cao that the player must accept or refuse; each changes what Guan Yu owes him.
segments.interactive_hook: Sets up the debt that the Huarong Road segment calls in.
key_choices: Accept or refuse the red horse
segments.canon_anchor: Guan Yu always leaves to find Liu Bei.

segments.title: Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage
segments.summary: Liu Bei visits the hermit Zhuge Liang three times in winter before he is received, and Zhuge Liang lays out his plan for dividing the empire.
segments.core_question: Will the Sleeping Dragon agree to serve you?
segments.why_this_template: Patience and sincerity with a man who is not even home at first; the player's behaviour on each visit decides how the final meeting goes.
segments.interactive_hook: The player feels the cost of waiting, and hears the Longzhong plan as a reward they earned.
key_choices: Wait in the snow or leave a letter
Stop Zhang Fei from burning the cottage
segments.canon_anchor: Zhuge Liang joins Liu Bei in every ending; what differs is how far he trusts him.

segments.title: The Ford at Changban
segments.summary: Zhao Yun rides back through Cao Cao's army to find Liu Bei's infant son, while Zhang Fei holds a bridge alone.
segments.core_question: Can you find the child and bring him out?
segments.why_this_template: Moving through a battlefield and choosing whom to ask and where to search.
segments.interactive_hook: A rescue told through choices, without combat detail.
key_choices: Search the village or the road
segments.canon_anchor: The child is always saved, as in the novel.

segments.title: The Stolen Letter
segments.summary: Cao Cao's envoy Jiang Gan visits his old friend Zhou Yu, steals a forged letter and carries it home, where it costs Cao Cao his two best admirals.
segments.core_question: What is Zhou Yu hiding, and should you trust what you find?
segments.why_this_template: The player investigates a camp at night and must judge whether evidence is planted.
segments.interactive_hook: A detective scene where the twist is that the player is the one being played.
segments.canon_anchor: Whatever the player decides, Cao Cao's admirals are lost before Red Cliffs.

segments.title: Arrows from the Fog
segments.summary: Ordered by Zhou Yu to deliver a hundred thousand arrows, Zhuge Liang promises them in three days, borrows boats from Lu Su and 'borrows' the arrows from Cao Cao in a fog.
segments.core_question: How do you get a hundred thousand arrows in three days without making any?
segments.why_this_template: The player gathers what they need, chooses when to sail, and runs the night raid step by step, with items and timing.
segments.interactive_hook: The joy of the stratagem: the player has to work out the fog, the straw and the drums, and the result is visible as a growing arrow count.
key_choices: Persuade Lu Su to keep your secret
segments.canon_anchor: If the raid fails, the next segment opens with Zhuge Liang having found the arrows another way; Red Cliffs goes ahead.

segments.title: The Huarong Road
segments.summary: After Red Cliffs, the beaten Cao Cao reaches the narrow Huarong Road and finds Guan Yu waiting for him, sworn on his life to take him.
segments.core_question: Do you keep your pledge or repay your debt?
segments.why_this_template: Two duties that cannot both be kept. The player hears out Cao Cao, looks at the men behind him, and decides.
segments.interactive_hook: A moral choice with real weight: the novel's own answer is one of several, and each ending says what it costs.
key_choices: Let them pass or take him
segments.canon_anchor: If Guan Yu takes Cao Cao, the next segment returns to the novel by having Cao Cao ransomed or escaping on the way to Liu Bei.

segments.title: The Borrowed Province
segments.summary: Lu Su comes again and again to ask for Jingzhou back, and Zhuge Liang finds a new reason to keep it each time.
segments.core_question: Can you get a straight answer out of Zhuge Liang?
